summary: Something the page needs to say about itself, in place — and that stays there.

pairs.dont: Use an Alert for something that just happened and does not need to persist.
pairs.do: Use Toast for a passing confirmation; keep Alert for a condition that is still true.
pairs.why: An Alert stays on the page. If the thing it describes is over, it becomes a piece of furniture people learn to read past.

pairs.dont: Use an Alert to ask a question that must be answered before continuing.
pairs.do: Use a Dialog when the work genuinely cannot proceed.
pairs.why: An Alert can be ignored by design. A question that cannot be ignored needs a control that takes the focus.

pairs.dont: Reach for Destructive because the message feels important.
pairs.do: Match the tone to the state: success happened, warning is about to, destructive already went wrong, info is context.
pairs.why: Four tones only work while they differ. A page of red alerts carries exactly as much information as a page of grey ones.

pairs.dont: State the problem and stop — "Connection failed."
pairs.do: Say what happened and what happens next, and attach the action if there is one.
pairs.why: An alert that cannot be acted on is a notification. The description is where the reader finds out whether this is theirs to fix.

pairs.dont: Let someone dismiss an alert describing a condition that is still true.
pairs.do: Offer dismiss for something acknowledged; leave a live condition on the page until it clears.
pairs.why: Dismissing is a promise that the information is no longer needed. If the disk is still full, closing the notice only hides it.

pairs.dont: Stack four alerts at the top of a page.
pairs.do: Show the one that matters, or summarise them into a single alert that links to the detail.
pairs.why: A stack of alerts reads as a wall. Whichever is most urgent is the one least likely to be read.

pairs.dont: Write a title that wraps onto a second line.
pairs.do: Keep the title to a short phrase and put the rest in the description.
pairs.why: The title shares its row with the icon and the dismiss. A wrapping title pushes them apart and stops the row reading as one thing.

a11y: No role by default, deliberately. role="alert" interrupts a screen reader mid-sentence — use it only for something that has just gone wrong, and role="status" for something that merely changed.
The leading icon is aria-hidden. Severity has to be in the words; colour and icon alone reach nobody using a screen reader.
The dismiss button's accessible name comes from dismissLabel. An X with no label announces nothing.
